title: Windows GPU unit tests job fails extracting OpenVINO packages due to locked tbb12.dll
signature: windows runner extract openvino packages expand-archive remove-item access to the path denied unauthorizedaccessexception locked dll file|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step fails: Expand-Archive cannot overwrite tbb12.dll because the file is locked by another process.

key_errors:
Remove-Item : Cannot remove item C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll:
Access to the path 'C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll' is denied.
At C:\Windows\system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\Modules\Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive\Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive.psm1:1029
+ ... Remove-Item -LiteralPath $currentArchiveEntryFileInfo.Ful ...
+ CategoryInfo : PermissionDenied: (C:\actions-runn...b\bin\tbb12.dll:FileInfo) [Remove-Item], UnauthorizedAccessException

##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
root_cause: The 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step runs 'Expand-Archive ... -Force' on a Windows self-hosted runner to overwrite a previous install directory. Expand-Archive's -Force first tries to delete the existing tbb12.dll before re-extracting it, but the DLL is still held open/locked by another process on the shared, persistent runner workspace (e.g. a lingering antivirus scan, a previous test process, or an OS file-indexer holding a handle), causing an UnauthorizedAccessException and failing the whole step with exit code 1. This is a long-running recurring infrastructure flake on this runner pool/workflow (now seen 10 times over the last ~1.5 days across many unrelated commits), not a code regression introduced by the triggering commit (which is a GPU debug-logging-only change).
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires the specific Windows self-hosted runner state (locked tbb12.dll handle); not reproducible from a clean local checkout. Can be approximated locally by holding tbb12.dll open (e.g. via a running process linked against it) and then running Expand-Archive -Force over the same path.
recommended_actions: Escalate to runner infra/DevOps: investigate why tbb12.dll remains locked between jobs on the Windows self-hosted runner pool used for 'GPU unit tests' (process handle leaks, AV scanning, workspace not fully cleaned between runs).

Consider replacing 'Expand-Archive -Force' with a step that first stops/ kills any lingering processes referencing the install directory, or that extracts to a fresh/unique directory per run instead of overwriting in place.
Add a retry-with-backoff wrapper around the extraction step as a stop-gap while the root lock cause is investigated.
Audit other steps/tools on this runner (antivirus, indexing service, residual test binaries) that could hold a handle on runtime/3rdparty/tbb/bin/tbb12.dll after a previous job.
prevention_strategies: Ensure Windows self-hosted runner workspaces are fully isolated/cleaned between jobs (e.g. ephemeral runners or forced process cleanup) so DLLs from a prior job are never left locked when the next job's extraction step runs. Add a pre-extraction step that explicitly releases handles (e.g. via handle.exe or process kill) on the install directory before Expand-Archive runs.
historical_context: Identical signature observed 9 times previously between 2026-11-09T16:30:00Z and 2026-11-10T19:25:24Z (see pattern 514ffa2ab52ad344), all on the 'Windows (VS 2022, Python 3.11, Release)' workflow's 'GPU unit tests' job, across many different commits — confirming this is a persistent runner-infrastructure issue unrelated to code changes.
